intro: The cabinet in the back corner of the arcade has been unplugged since 1987, but nobody has ever moved it. Its high-score table is really a visitors' book, and the little signatures in it keep changing as if the machine were still taking turns. The regulars do not mention it over the hum of the fruit machines; they just leave a coin on the marquee and watch the screen hold its breath. The leather ledger under the coin door keeps a register of monograms, each closed by the same curved stroke, and the hinge will not lift until they have all been pressed flat together.
echo: Up close, every face on the screen is made of tiny squares.

puzzles.title: Player Two
puzzles.flavor: Bunting on the halyard, and not for a celebration.
hints: Ships carry a flag for every letter of the alphabet. Do you know them?

puzzles.title: Speedrun
puzzles.flavor: Each entry picked up a hitchhiker on the way.
hints: Each jumble is almost a word from this round, but with a letter to spare. Which letter, every time?

puzzles.title: Continue?
puzzles.flavor: It goes round and round, and only gets anywhere in the middle.
hints: All the letters of a sentence are here, but not in rows. Try walking the grid the way a snail would.

puzzles.title: Extra Life
puzzles.flavor: Everyone has a place. Everyone pays for it in their own name.

clues: Exactly one person sits between Daniel and Griselda.
Cordelia sits somewhere between Cedric and Daniel.
Cordelia sits immediately to the right of Cedric.
Exactly 3 people sit between Cordelia and Daniel.
Griselda sits somewhere between Cedric and Justine.
Exactly 3 people sit between Cedric and Malcolm.

hints: Only one arrangement satisfies every clue; start from whoever has an end seat or a fixed neighbour. Once they're seated, why might the seat numbers matter?

puzzles.title: High Score
puzzles.flavor: Two kinds of footprint on the sand, in no particular hurry.
hints: Only two kinds of mark, in groups of one to four. Which old alphabet is built from exactly that?

puzzles.title: Kill Screen
puzzles.flavor: Only one page survived. It was the only page anyone needed.

blocks.text: The cabinet in the back corner of the arcade has been unplugged since 1987. It still has a high-score table, and the initials on it keep changing.

hints: The first number in each pair never goes past the number of words on the page. What does the second count?

meta.title: Meta: Insert Coin
meta.flavor: The last lock takes every signature at once.
hints: Blaise de Vigenère needed a key to open this. Has every answer signed its work?
